results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 58 prose/list units align one-to-one with spec paragraphs p01-p57 in spec order (structure check passed), and each outline summary matches its paragraph's controlling idea, including the moved polygons-before-clustering order and p24a/p47.

results.quote: the map is another such surface
results.finding: The paragraph states the map-needs-its-own-ranking claim in its first sentence, argues place-first, restates the same claim, then ends on a third idea (Part IV's compile-into-structure thesis). The spec's controlling idea is one causal chain (place leads, so the map needs its own ranking and evaluation) and its transition_in says the claim for the map is stated after the place-first argument; the opening clause anticipates it, so the outliner needed two summaries.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: The Polygon Problem at Hearthly ¶4
results.finding: Both clauses (list-shaped sizing, cross-cloud pans) are subordinate to the opening sentence 'Tomasz's worry is that Hearthly's traffic does not fit the shared platform', matching the spec's single controlling idea.

results.draft_locus: The Map Is a Different Product ¶3
results.finding: 'Two consequences follow' frames both consequences as one idea, exactly as the spec's controlling idea declares.

results.draft_locus: Clustering: Three Ways to Show Ten Thousand Results ¶3
results.finding: The zoom-level split and the H3 hexagon remark both describe how the approaches are combined in practice; the spec's controlling idea declares both, and the hexagon sentence is short and subordinate.
Every unit ties to at least one of S1-S6 as declared in the spec; no orphan paragraph (Vertical Differences' Motorvane engine note supports S6's shared-compiler claim).

Each table (five ways, list vs map, clustering approaches, commute patterns, trade-offs, verticals), figure (1-5) and source is followed or framed by a sentence saying what it shows. Arithmetic checks: 10% of 2,700 = 270/s; 30% miss of 270 = 81 ~ 80 isochrones/s; 270 x 50 x 1-2 places = 13,500-27,000 matrix elements/s; polygon 146->31 median, 2,000->64 cap, p99 1.8 s->240 ms consistent with Figure 3; €389,000 within Valuo €372,000-401,000 and under Sophie's €400,000 cap; H3 res 7 edge ~1.4 km, res 8 ~0.74 km², res 9 ~0.1 km²/~200 m consistent.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary (e.g. 'Two complaints arrive with the numbers', 'Ingrid's second question', 'Ingrid's third question needs a second polygon', 'With the cache in place, the commute arithmetic', 'The table hides one cross-cutting cost', 'Ingrid's three questions have one answer'). Weakest but acceptable: 'The five expressions meet buyers on the map' (both flow readers: thin but works) and the Five Ways opening, which picks up Ingrid's first question only through 'a different index primitive'.

Both flow readers state an organising principle that agrees with the declared pattern (problem posed by the scene's three questions, prerequisite vocabulary, then the compiler and its parts large-to-small, then peak load, worked example and judgement sections), say the roadmap announces it and the chapter keeps to it, and mark no section unclear. P3/P4/P5, H3 and Common Ground (A3/B4, A4/B2, A11/B10) are on audience.already_knows, so not counted as lost-thread points for the declared reader.

results.quote: So the map, like the recommendation surfaces, needs its own ranking and evaluation
results.finding: Flow reader A (A1): the restated ranking claim after the place-first examples 'made me check whether this was a new point... the paragraph runs in a loop'; A2 adds that the closing Part IV compile sentence reads as 'a second, separate ending'. The spec's order (claim after the place-first argument) is fine; the draft states the claim twice.

results.draft_locus: Commute Search: Isochrones and Travel Times ¶2
results.quote: Behind both forms sit two patterns, which a platform will usually need together; My Places is per-listing travel time.
results.finding: Flow reader A (A5): 'It was unclear whether forms and patterns are the same two things'; the tail maps Rightmove's form to one pattern and leaves Zillow's unmapped. The spec's order (forms, then the patterns behind them) is fine; the bridging sentence does not say how the two forms relate to the two patterns.

results.draft_locus: Commute Search: Isochrones and Travel Times ¶8
results.quote: If each matrix times 50 pins (the largest list page) to one or two of the user's places
results.finding: Flow reader A (A6): the sentence is ungrammatical and 'I had to rebuild the arithmetic'; 'the largest list page' brings a list concept into a map-pin calculation. A7 adds that the paragraph does not say which stream (isochrones or matrices) drives which half of the routing choice. The arithmetic itself is correct.

results.draft_locus: Performance and Caching at the Peak ¶2
results.quote: **Approximate counts** and separate request paths for counts, clusters and the side list.
results.finding: Flow reader B (B7): levers 1 and 3 repeat choices 2 and 3 of 'A pan, a zoom, a count' and 'made me check whether something new was being said. Nothing was.' The spec deliberately revisits them as peak levers after all parts are described; the draft restates them without pointing back, so the fix is a back-reference (e.g. 'the snapping and count split from the architecture section, now as levers'), not a reorder.

results.draft_locus: Worked Example: The Lyon Apartment on the Map ¶1
results.quote: In May 2027, a three-room (T3) **68 m²** flat in Lyon 7e is listed for sale
results.finding: Flow reader B (B8): after a scene set in late September 2027, the May 2027 date 'looked like a mistake until the next paragraph explained that this is a walk-through of a past session through the target design'. Reader A (A8) re-read the framing sentence of the next paragraph to place three time frames. The spec's dates are fine; the walk-through framing comes after the date instead of before it.

results.quote: its main geo query is a radius around the buyer's postcode in German (*Umkreissuche*)
results.finding: Flow reader A (A9): 'In German attaches awkwardly and reads at first as if the postcode were in German'; A9 also notes 'As the table below shows' leans on a table not yet seen and the Motorvane engine sentence feels off topic.

results.quote: Real estate shown at the exact address has no coarse point.
results.finding: Flow reader B (B3): 'I had to re-read it to see that it means "so the problem does not arise for real estate"'; the sentence sits between the goods case and the in-between case without a connective. Reported by one reader only.

Every does_not_know term is given before or at first use: bounding box, map tile and isochrone (Five Ways definitions; isochrone search glossed in Introduction ¶2), geo clustering (Introduction ¶2, Clustering ¶1), zoom/x/y tiles and geotile_grid, vector tiles (clustering table), geo_point/geo_shape and BKD tree, Douglas-Peucker simplification, travel-time matrix (commute table), Valhalla and GTFS, routing terms. P0-P5, H3, Common Ground, Motorvane are on already_knows.

results.draft_locus: The Map Is a Different Product ¶1
results.quote: uses S2 cells as a location feature
results.finding: S2 cells are used here and again in Drawn Polygons step 6 ('H3 or S2 cells') without a gloss; S2 is on neither already_knows (which has H3) nor explained in the chapter. No flow reader reported it, so it is minor.
Opens with a direct statement tied to the previous chapter and concrete place-first examples; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.
Conclusion answers the scene's questions with a synthesis and hands off; no 'in conclusion', no new subtopic, no body evidence, not a bare restated thesis.

States what no single section states (the component that fixes the 1.8-second polygons is the same one that enforces the public-point rule, the single pin and the isochrone cache) and why it matters (Hearthly moves onto the shared platform without The Forced Fit; new place interfaces need no per-client geo logic).
Returns to the scene: Ingrid's three questions, the 1.8-second polygons, Agence Rhône Habitat's flat; the routing quote is answered as 'routing is bought on a forecast of peak volumes'.

The opening-only reader predicted every roadmap promise in order (case and three questions, five ways, map as a different product, compiler and its parts, peak performance, Lyon walk-through, trade-offs/verticals/failure modes/CA view/questions) and the evidence (Airbnb, Zillow, Rightmove, engine and routing docs, fictional Veldmark).

Reader gives the compiler in front of the engine with polygon repair/simplify/cap, tile snapping and place-ID filters; public-point pins counted per canonical property (one pin, three offers); cached isochrones keyed by snapped origin plus matrices for pins on screen; routing chosen on a forecast of peak isochrone and matrix volumes against pricing and license, per-request growing with campaigns vs fixed license/self-hosted as capacity planning. Platform ownership of the compiler is implied rather than stated; acceptable.

Reader names the front-door leak via clusters of one, fine heatmap grids and vector-tile hits; the public-point rule for every returned geometry, deterministic public point, API cannot read the exact point, minimum counts per cell, and DPO-signed platform invariant. Matches expected.

Reader explains attention follows geography, ranking moves to pin selection, cites Airbnb 2024 and 2025 (~80%, list NDCG fails), states the property-portal application is the author's inference, and gives contacts/saves per map session and time to shortlist. Matches expected.
